name: Proto-Earth, ~4.55 Ga
sub: before the Moon-forming impact; a guessed air of ~3 bar CO2 over 1 bar N2, with impact dust; the young Sun at 17 Myr
note: No constraint exists on the air before the last giant impact. Sun: Baraffe et al. 2015 1 Msun track at 17 Myr (4614 K, log L -0.327)

name: Early Hadean, ~4.50 Ga
sub: ~10 Myr after the Moon-forming impact: magma ocean frozen, ~30 bar CO2 left; Moon at ~8 Earth radii
note: CO2 tens to ~100 bar after the impact (Zahnle et al. 2010); Rayleigh optical depth ~5 at 550 nm. Sun: Baraffe et al. 2015 1 Msun track at 67 Myr (5532 K, log L -0.167)

name: Late Hadean, ~4.0 Ga
sub: CO2 mostly drawn down into carbonate; ~1 bar N2, ~0.5 bar CO2

name: Early Archean, ~3.8 Ga
sub: haze-free, anoxic; CO2 ~0.1 bar, CH4 ~1000 ppm, no ozone

name: Neoarchean, ~2.7 Ga (clear)
sub: haze-free between haze episodes: CH4/CO2 ~0.06, below the ~0.1 at which haze forms
note: The background the sulfur and carbon isotope records return to between haze episodes (Zerkle et al. 2012; Izon et al. 2015)

name: Neoarchean haze episode, ~2.58 Ga (thin haze)
sub: CH4/CO2 ~0.2: the stable thin organic haze of Zerkle et al. 2012, tau(550nm)~0.15
note: Zerkle et al. 2012: above CH4/CO2 ~0.1 a haze forms and runs up to a stable ~0.2, beyond which no biological flux can push it

name: Neoarchean haze episode, ~2.52 Ga (thick haze)
sub: "Pale Orange Dot": Titan-like fractal organic haze, tau(550nm)~0.6

name: Neoarchean haze episode, ~2.52 Ga (very thick haze, upper bound)
sub: the thick episode at the upper end of plausible haze, tau(550nm)~1.5: CH4/CO2 ~0.2; in the report only

name: Paleoproterozoic, ~2.2 Ga
sub: after the Great Oxidation Event: O2 ~1% PAL, ozone column 66 DU
note: Cooke et al. 2022 global-mean column at 1% of present O2: 66 DU

name: Snowball Earth, ~700 Ma
sub: the Sturtian glaciation, 717-661 Ma: cold, dry, very clean air over ice (albedo 0.75); ozone 169 DU
note: Cooke et al. 2022 global-mean column at 10% of present O2: 169 DU, nearest this epoch

name: Cryogenian, ~650 Ma (between the snowballs)
sub: the open sea and bare land between the Sturtian and Marinoan glaciations: O2 ~10% PAL, ozone 169 DU
note: The 22 Myr between the Sturtian (717-661 Ma) and Marinoan (639-635 Ma) glaciations (Rooney et al. 2020; Tasistro-Hart et al. 2025): the snowball air without its ice. Cooke et al. 2022 global-mean column at 10% of present O2: 169 DU

name: Ordovician meteor storm, ~466 Ma
sub: after the L-chondrite parent body broke up: O2 ~17%, CO2 ~2,500 ppm, a little meteoric dust aloft
note: O2 at about 80% of today (Krause et al. 2018); Cooke et al. 2022 columns near this level are within a few percent of today, so the modern latitude columns are scaled by 0.97

name: Carboniferous, ~300 Ma
sub: O2 ~30-35%; total pressure ~1.1 bar; wildfire smoke common
note: Cooke et al. 2022 state a pre-industrial global mean of 279 DU. The 150% PAL mean is not given in the text; the columns here are the modern ones scaled by 300/279, for a mean near 300 DU

name: K-Pg impact winter, 66 Ma
sub: months after Chicxulub: stratospheric soot (tau~1.5) + sulfate (tau~0.5)

name: Volcanic year, 1816 (Tambora)
sub: the stratospheric sulfate veil of Tambora (April 1815) through 1816, tau(550nm)~0.4

name: Ozone-hole spring
sub: Antarctic spring in the ozone-hole years: column 130 DU
note: Polar-spring column in the 100-150 DU range of the Antarctic ozone hole; layer centered near 18 km

name: Modern, clean air
sub: aerosol optical depth 0.1; ozone 260/300/330 DU by latitude
note: Equatorial minimum, mid-latitude 300 DU, polar-summer 330 DU; a tenth of the column is tropospheric

name: Year 2100
sub: today's clean air, with the filed megaconstellation and the Sunrise orbital datacenters
note: Same air as the modern clean sky. The satellites are drawn in the site, not in the radiative transfer.
